Rating notch change (Watchlist POC — one task)

Source: POC_Requirements_v0.2_EN.md (Corporate Client Credit Monitoring — Watchlist Tool).
This job is a one-requirement slice of that document: the notch change that Indicators 11, 12 and 13 and the notch
calculator (REQ-06-02) are built on. It is small: one card.

## Requirement

| Req ID | Requirement | Acceptance Criteria (summary) |
|---|---|---|
| REQ-06-02 (part) | Given a previous and a current rating, the system computes the notch change between them | BBB+ → BB+ = 3-notch downgrade; BB+ → BBB+ = 3-notch upgrade; A → A = 0 |

## Clarifications for this slice (confirmed by the business unit)

- C1. Rating scale, best to worst (19 steps): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-.
  A notch is one step on this scale. Input is trimmed with `String.prototype.trim()` and case-insensitive ("bbb+" = "BBB+").
- C2. Every invalid input (an unknown rating, an empty string, a non-string) is rejected with a RangeError. A String object
  such as `new String('A')` is a non-string. No banking-regulation or internal-policy constraint applies to this slice.
- C3. The result is signed: downgrade positive, upgrade negative, unchanged 0.
- C4. No UI, CLI or printed output; other parts of the POC import the function.

## Contract

- `src/ratings/notch.mjs`
  - `RATING_SCALE` — the 19 ratings of C1, best first.
  - `notchChange(previous, current)` → integer (C3).

Plain Node ESM, no dependencies; tests with `node --test` next to the code under `test/`.

## Staffing

- The backend developer works on the **haiku** model.

dl — the deterministic half of the /deliver flow.
The board, phase transitions, worktrees, gates, reviews and merges are run by this script, not by the LLM.
Michael (the orchestrator) calls these commands through Bash; you can call them from a terminal too.
Every transition is checked here: a model cannot skip a gate, merge an unreviewed card or exceed the limits.

  dl [-C <repo>] <command> …     -C (or DELIVER_REPO) = run against that repo from any directory

  dl new "<title>" "<request>"   new job: .work/<JOB>/, job/<JOB> branch, integration worktree
  dl status                      active job's phase + board table + next actions
  dl next                        the next actions the flow requires, one per line (ACTION args)
  dl board                       board table only
  dl phase <phase>               set phase (intake readiness awaiting_clarification planning awaiting_plan_approval executing
                                 integrating closing awaiting_pr_merge done aborted) — guarded
  dl jobset '<jq expr>'          update job.json            e.g. dl jobset '.stack=["typescript","react"]'
  dl readiness                   check the requirements readiness review (readiness.json → readiness.md, QUESTIONS.md)
  dl clarify <id> "<answer>"     record the human's answer to an open business question (human only)
  dl decide <id> "<decision>" "<rationale>"   the PM closes an open implementation-detail item (owner pm)
  dl unfreeze "<reason>"         (human, terminal only) reopen the decisions frozen at planning
  dl reseal "<reason>"           (human, terminal only) accept an edit made to job.json/board.json outside dl
  dl roles                       check job.roles against roles.yaml and generate the project's role cards
                                 (.work/<job>/roles/*.md, ROLES.md) — runs on dl phase planning
  dl learn <role|all> "<lesson>" --topic <slug> (--card T-xx | --evidence "…") [--scope project|shared|kit]
                                 propose a lesson, with what happened; it reaches .deliver/knowledge/ with this job's PR
  dl followup "<finding>" [--card T-xx]   a defect seen outside the job's scope — listed in the PR
  dl knowledge [list|topics|promote <topic> "<rule>"|sync-md]   standards + lessons for the role cards; promote = a new
                                 standard (with the PR); sync-md → Munder Difflin knowledge graph
  dl validate                    board.json schema + dependency + scope-overlap check
  dl ready                       ids of cards that may be dispatched now (deps merged, attempts left)
  dl wt add <card> [--resume]    card worktree + state=running + attempts+1 (--resume: no bump, after a restart)
  dl wt rm <card>                remove the card worktree (branch is kept)
  dl card <card> state <state>   review | blocked | ready (from blocked) | archived ["<reason>" — required after the start]
  dl card <card> note "<text>"   attach a note to a card (blocked reason, guidance, …)
  dl reopen <id> "<why>"         before the freeze: an answer that does not answer its question goes back to the human
  dl pm-decide "<what>" "<why>" [card]   after the start the human is not asked: your decision, logged, listed in the PR
  dl card <card> retry           human-granted: attempts=0 and state=ready (after guidance)
  dl card <card> set <field> <value> "<reason>"   change a ready/blocked card's contract (validated, logged, history)
  dl card add <card.json> "<reason>"              add a card (e.g. a fix card) — gets the next id, validated, logged
  dl gate <card>                 mechanical gate: right branch, clean tree, commits, in scope, verify passes
  dl qa <card> pass|fail "<summary>"   record the QA/Test verdict on the card's acceptance criteria
                                 (needs a passed gate on the current commit)
  dl review <card> approve|changes "<summary>" [--by <role>]   record a reviewer's verdict (needs gate PASS + QA pass);
                                 a card with "reviewers": [...] needs every one of them to approve the same commit
  dl integrate <card>            --no-ff merge into the job branch → merged (needs gate PASS + QA pass +
                                 review approve, all on the current commit; exit 3 on conflict, 5 when the
                                 repo's commit rules refuse the merge message)
  dl verify-all                  run verify_full in the integration worktree
  dl ship                        deliver per merge_mode: human|semi|auto → push + PR (+ auto-merge / merge on green),
                                 local → merge into the base branch. Needs verify-all PASS + report.md (phase closing)
  dl pr                          PR state (awaiting_pr_merge): merged → done; closed → aborted; open → checks/review
  dl approve plan [note]         record the human's plan approval (only when gates.plan is on; off by default)
  dl reject  plan "<note>"       record the human's rejection of the plan
  dl md-dispatch <card> <prompt-file>   Munder Difflin: run the card's dev as a worker on the floor
  dl md-hire                     Munder Difflin: seat one person per role seat (job.roles[].count) — the whole job
  dl md-seats                    who sits where: pending / starting / live / gone / failed (with why), each seat's open task
  dl config [--init]            the settings that apply in this repo (kit defaults ⊕ ~/.deliver/config.json ⊕ .deliver.json)
  dl floor-open "<request>"     /deliver from a terminal in a floor repo: open Munder Difflin on its floor, hand Michael the job
  dl dispatch munder|subagent "<why>"   (human) switch how this job's roles run: floor seats (default) or subagents
  dl md-reseat <seat> "<why>" [--model m]   a failed or stuck seat gets a new person (another model for a credit error);
                                 also spelled dl md-hire --reseat <seat>
  dl md-send <seat|role> <task> <prompt-file> [--agent a]   a work order to a seat: role card + agent instructions + task

# Role catalog — Michael selects roles ONLY from this list (not from all of ECC's agents).
# `dl roles` turns the selected roles into project-specific role cards (.work/<job>/roles/<role>.md); on the Munder
# Difflin floor every seat of a role is a person (dl md-hire). A role card = rules.all + rules.<kind> + the role's own
# rules + project facts.
#
# Format (kept to a small YAML subset so bin/roles.mjs can read it without dependencies):
#   2-space indentation · `key: value` · `- item` lists · "double-quoted" or bare scalars · `#` comments
#
# kind:     ba | lead | dev | review | qa      (Michael himself is the PM/orchestrator)

8	
9	| Req ID | Requirement | Acceptance Criteria (summary) |
10	|---|---|---|
11	| REQ-06-02 (part) | Given a previous and a current rating, the system computes the notch change between them | BBB+ → BB+ = 3-notch downgrade; BB+ → BBB+ = 3-notch upgrade; A → A = 0 |
12	
13	## Clarifications for this slice (confirmed by the business unit)
14	
15	- C1. Rating scale, best to worst (19 steps): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-.
16	  A notch is one step on this scale. Input is trimmed with `String.prototype.trim()` and case-insensitive ("bbb+" = "BBB+").
17	- C2. Every invalid input (an unknown rating, an empty string, a non-string) is rejected with a RangeError. A String object
18	  such as `new String('A')` is a non-string. No banking-regulation or internal-policy constraint applies to this slice.
19	- C3. The result is signed: downgrade positive, upgrade negative, unchanged 0.
20	- C4. No UI, CLI or printed output; other parts of the POC import the function.
21

24	- `src/ratings/notch.mjs`
25	  - `RATING_SCALE` — the 19 ratings of C1, best first.
26	  - `notchChange(previous, current)` → integer (C3).
27	
28	Plain Node ESM, no dependencies; tests with `node --test` next to the code under `test/`.

summary:
# Plan

## Goal

Deliver the notch-change primitive for the Watchlist POC: a pure, synchronous ES module `src/ratings/notch.mjs` that exports `RATING_SCALE` (the 19 C1 ratings, best first, frozen) and `notchChange(previous, current)`. `notchChange` returns the signed number of steps from `previous` to `current`: downgrade is positive, upgrade is negative, unchanged is 0. Any invalid input throws a `RangeError`. Indicators 11, 12 and 13 and the full REQ-06-02 notch calculator will be built on this later (readiness PRD-goal). The work is done when every AC below passes under `npm test` (`node --test`) (readiness DEL-ci).

## Scope

- One card, one component: `ratings` (library, node). Code goes in `src/ratings/notch.mjs`. Developer unit tests go in `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`. QA's consumer-level tests go in `test/integration/ratings/` (readiness ARC-components, TST-strategy).
- `RATING_SCALE` is a frozen array of the 19 ratings in C1 order (readiness CON-interface, X-scale-immutability).
- `notchChange(previous, current)` returns `index(current) - index(previous)` after `String.prototype.trim()` and case-insensitive matching (REQ-06-02, C1, C3).
- Input validation: each argument is rejected with a `RangeError` for every C2 class. `previous` is validated before `current`, and the error message is built safely (C2, readiness CON-errors, X-error-message).
- Inline JSDoc on both exports covering the sign convention and the `RangeError` (readiness DEL-docs).
- Plain Node 18+ ESM. No dependencies, no imports, no I/O, no console output (CLAUDE.md, C4).

## Out of scope

- Indicators 11, 12 and 13, the rest of REQ-06-02 (the notch calculator itself), and every other POC requirement (readiness PRD-scope).
- Ratings outside the 19-step scale (CC, C, D, NR, SD, etc.). Callers get a `RangeError` for these; there is no mapping or fallback.
- Any UI, CLI, printed or logged output, persistence, rating sources or external systems (C4, readiness ARC-data, ARC-integration, NFR-observability).
- Converting non-primitive inputs: String objects, arrays and objects with `toString` are never coerced (C2).
- Asserting the exact text of the error message. Only the error type is asserted (X-error-message).
- README, changelog or runbook changes (readiness DEL-docs).
- Performance targets (readiness NFR-performance) and banking-regulation or internal-policy constraints (C2, readiness NFR-compliance).

## Acceptance criteria

Notation: `S` = the imported `RATING_SCALE`. Index 0 = `AAA` … index 18 = `CCC-`. Equality checks use `assert.strictEqual` (Object.is semantics).

### Contract and scale

**AC-1 (Contract; C1; X-scale-immutability): scale content and order**
- Given `import { RATING_SCALE } from './src/ratings/notch.mjs'`,
- when it is read,
- then `Array.isArray(RATING_SCALE) === true`, `RATING_SCALE.length === 19`, and `assert.deepStrictEqual(RATING_SCALE, ['AAA','AA+','AA','AA-','A+','A','A-','BBB+','BBB','BBB-','BB+','BB','BB-','B+','B','B-','CCC+','CCC','CCC-'])`. Every element is a primitive string with ASCII `+` (U+002B) and `-` (U+002D).

**AC-2 (X-scale-immutability; C1): scale is frozen**
- Given the imported `RATING_SCALE`,
- when `Object.isFrozen(RATING_SCALE)` is checked and, in strict-mode test code, `RATING_SCALE.push('CC')`, `RATING_SCALE[0] = 'X'`, `RATING_SCALE.length = 0` and `RATING_SCALE.reverse()` are each tried,
- then `Object.isFrozen` returns `true` and each mutation throws `TypeError`.
- Afterwards `RATING_SCALE[0] === 'AAA'`, `RATING_SCALE.length === 19` and `notchChange('AAA','CCC-') === 18`.

**AC-3 (Contract; C3; readiness ARC-async): return type**
- Given valid inputs `('BBB+','BB+')`,
- when `notchChange` is called,
- then the result is not a Promise, `typeof result === 'number'` and `Number.isInteger(result) === true`.
- For `('A','A')` the result is `+0`: `Object.is(result, 0) === true`, never `-0`.

### REQ-06-02 examples

**AC-4 (REQ-06-02; C3): downgrade.** Given `previous = 'BBB+'` and `current = 'BB+'`, when `notchChange('BBB+','BB+')` is called, then it returns `3`.

**AC-5 (REQ-06-02; C3): upgrade.** Given `previous = 'BB+'` and `current = 'BBB+'`, when `notchChange('BB+','BBB+')` is called, then it returns `-3`.

**AC-6 (REQ-06-02; C3): unchanged.** Given `previous = 'A'` and `current = 'A'`, when `notchChange('A','A')` is called, then it returns `0`.

### Full scale (X-test-coverage)

**AC-7 (C1; C3): every pair**
- Given every pair `(i, j)` with `i, j ∈ 0..18` (361 pairs),
- when `notchChange(S[i], S[j])` is called,
- then it returns `j - i`. This includes `0` for all 19 cases where `i === j`, and `notchChange(a,b) === -notchChange(b,a)` for every pair.

**AC-8 (C1; C3): adjacent steps**
- Given each of the 18 adjacent pairs (`AAA→AA+`, `AA+→AA`, `AA→AA-`, `AA-→A+`, `A+→A`, `A→A-`, `A-→BBB+`, `BBB+→BBB`, `BBB→BBB-`, `BBB-→BB+`, `BB+→BB`, `BB→BB-`, `BB-→B+`, `B+→B`, `B→B-`, `B-→CCC+`, `CCC+→CCC`, `CCC→CCC-`),
- when `notchChange(worse_after_better)` is called (`notchChange(S[i], S[i+1])`),
- then it returns `1`. The reverse `notchChange(S[i+1], S[i])` returns `-1`.

**AC-9 (C1; C3): extremes**
- Given the ends of the scale,
- when `notchChange('AAA','CCC-')` and `notchChange('CCC-','AAA')` are called,
- then they return `18` and `-18`.
- No pair of valid inputs gives a value outside `-18..18`.

### Trim and case (C1)

**AC-10 (C1): trimming**
- Given padded inputs,
- when they are passed to `notchChange`, then they behave exactly like the trimmed rating:

| Call | Expected |
|---|---|
| `notchChange(' BBB+ ', 'BB+')` | `3` |
| `notchChange('BB+', '\tBBB+\n')` | `-3` |
| `notchChange('\u00A0A\u00A0', 'A')` (NBSP, removed by `trim()`) | `0` |
| `notchChange('\r\n AAA', 'CCC- \uFEFF')` | `18` |

**AC-11 (C1): case-insensitivity**
- Given lower- or mixed-case inputs,
- when they are passed to `notchChange`, then they match the upper-case rating:

| Call | Expected |
|---|---|
| `notchChange('bbb+', 'BBB+')` | `0` |
| `notchChange('bbb+', 'bb+')` | `3` |
| `notchChange('Bb+', ' bBb+ ')` | `-3` |
| `notchChange('aaa', 'ccc-')` | `18` |
| `notchChange('aA-', 'AA-')` | `0` |

Trim and case-folding also apply to every rating in AC-7. For example, `notchChange(S[i].toLowerCase(), ' ' + S[j] + ' ')` returns `j - i`.

### Invalid input (C2; readiness CON-errors). Every value is checked in both argument positions

For each value `v` in the classes below, both `notchChange(v, 'A')` and `notchChange('A', v)` must throw a `RangeError`, checked with `assert.throws(fn, RangeError)`. Neither call may return a value, and neither may throw a `TypeError` or any other error type.

**AC-12 (C2): non-string primitives**
- Given `v` ∈ {`undefined`, `null`, `0`, `7`, `3.5`, `NaN`, `true`, `false`, `1n`, `Symbol('A')`},
- when called as above,
- then a `RangeError` is thrown.
- The missing-argument forms are covered too: `notchChange()` and `notchChange('A')` throw `RangeError`.

**AC-13 (C2): non-string objects, including String objects**
- Given `v` ∈ {`new String('A')`, `new String('BBB+')`, `['A']`, `[]`, `{}`, `{ toString() { return 'A'; } }`, `Object.create(null)`, `() => 'A'`, `new Date(0)`},
- when called as above,
- then a `RangeError` is thrown.
- `new String('A')` and `['A']` are not coerced, even though `String(v) === 'A'`.

**AC-14 (C2): empty and whitespace-only strings**
- Given `v` ∈ {`''`, `' '`, `'\t\n'`, `'\u00A0'`},
- when called as above,
- then a `RangeError` is thrown.

**AC-15 (C2; C1): unknown ratings**
- Given `v` ∈ {`'CC'`, `'C'`, `'D'`, `'NR'`, `'SD'`, `'BBB++'`, `'AAAA'`, `'BBB +'` (internal space), `'B B'`, `'A\u2212'` (Unicode minus), `'A\uFF0B'` (fullwidth plus), `'constructor'`, `'__proto__'`, `'toString'`},
- when called as above,
- then a `RangeError` is thrown.

**AC-16 (C2; X-error-message): both arguments invalid, and message safety**
- Given both arguments are invalid, e.g. `(Symbol('x'), 42)`, `(null, 'CC')`, `('', Symbol('y'))` and `(Object.create(null), new String('A'))`,
- when `notchChange` is called,
- then it throws a `RangeError`. Building the message must never raise a different error. In particular a Symbol or `Object.create(null)` in either position still gives a `RangeError`, not a `TypeError`.
- `previous` is validated before `current`, so the message names `previous`. The tests assert only the error type (X-error-message). The check order and the message wording (argument name, `typeof` for non-strings) are confirmed in code review.

### Purity (C4; CLAUDE.md)

**AC-17 (C4; CLAUDE.md): no imports, I/O or output**
- Given `src/ratings/notch.mjs`,
- when it is inspected with `grep -nE "^\s*import|require\(|console\.|process\." src/ratings/notch.mjs`,
- then nothing matches.
- Calling `notchChange` on valid and invalid inputs writes nothing to stdout or stderr. `package.json` gains no `dependencies` or `devDependencies`.

**AC-18 (readiness DEL-ci; TST-strategy): test run and file locations**
- Given the delivered card,
- when `npm test` runs from the repo root,
- then it exits 0. The run includes `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` and the QA tests under `test/integration/ratings/`, which together cover AC-1 to AC-16.

## Risks and assumptions

**Risks.** These are the likely mistakes, since the developer runs on the haiku model.
- Calling `.trim()` or `.toUpperCase()` before the type check. This turns non-strings into a `TypeError` (AC-12) or coerces `new String('A')` and `['A']` into valid ratings (AC-13). The check must be `typeof v === 'string'`.
- Building the message with `'…' + value` or a template literal. This throws a `TypeError` for Symbols and for `Object.create(null)` (AC-16).
- Looking ratings up in a plain object map. Prototype keys can then match (AC-15 `'constructor'`, `'__proto__'`). Looking up the index in the frozen array avoids this.
- Reversing the sign (`previous - current`). AC-4 and AC-5 catch it.
- Writing the scale with typographic minus or plus signs. AC-1 checks the code points.

**Assumptions.**
- The contract needs only the two named exports. It neither requires nor forbids a default export, so none is planned.
- Extra arguments beyond two are ignored. The request is silent on them and it does not change the result for valid calls.
- "Whitespace" means exactly what `String.prototype.trim()` removes (ECMAScript WhiteSpace and LineTerminator, including NBSP and BOM), as C1 states.
- The examples were checked against C1 (BBB+ = 7, BB+ = 10). With C3's sign they agree, so there is no contradiction (readiness PRD-conflicts).
- `RangeError` for non-strings, rather than the usual `TypeError`, is deliberate and binding (C2).

## Open questions

None. All 30 readiness items are decided or not applicable. The three PM decisions (X-scale-immutability, X-error-message, X-test-coverage) are applied above and do not change scope.

Every element is a primitive string with ASCII `+` (U+002B) and `-` (U+002D).

**AC-2 (X-scale-immutability; C1): scale is frozen**
- Given the imported `RATING_SCALE`,
- when `Object.isFrozen(RATING_SCALE)` is checked and, in strict-mode test code, `RATING_SCALE.push('CC')`, `RATING_SCALE[0] = 'X'`, `RATING_SCALE.length = 0` and `RATING_SCALE.reverse()` are each tried,
- then `Object.isFrozen` returns `true` and each mutation throws `TypeError`.
- Afterwards `RATING_SCALE[0] === 'AAA'`, `RATING_SCALE.length === 19` and `notchChange('AAA','CCC-') === 18`.

**AC-3 (Contract; C3; readiness ARC-async): return type**
- Given valid inputs `('BBB+','BB+')`,
- when `notchChange` is called,
- then the result is not a Promise, `typeof result === 'number'` and `Number.isInteger(result) === true`.
- For `('A','A')` the result is `+0`: `Object.is(result, 0) === true`, never `-0`.

### REQ-06-02 examples

**AC-4 (REQ-06-02; C3): downgrade.** Given `previous = 'BBB+'` and `current = 'BB+'`, when `notchChange('BBB+','BB+')` is called, then it returns `3`.

**AC-5 (REQ-06-02; C3): upgrade.** Given `previous = 'BB+'` and `current = 'BBB+'`, when `notchChange('BB+','BBB+')` is called, then it returns `-3`.

**AC-6 (REQ-06-02; C3): unchanged.** Given `previous = 'A'` and `current = 'A'`, when `notchChange('A','A')` is called, then it returns `0`.

### Full scale (X-test-coverage)

**AC-7 (C1; C3): every pair**
- Given every pair `(i, j)` with `i, j ∈ 0..18` (361 pairs),
- when `notchChange(S[i], S[j])` is called,
- then it returns `j - i`. This includes `0` for all 19 cases where `i === j`, and `notchChange(a,b) === -notchChange(b,a)` for every pair.

**AC-8 (C1; C3): adjacent steps**
- Given each of the 18 adjacent pairs (`AAA→AA+`, `AA+→AA`, `AA→AA-`, `AA-→A+`, `A+→A`, `A→A-`, `A-→BBB+`, `BBB+→BBB`, `BBB→BBB-`, `BBB-→BB+`, `BB+→BB`, `BB→BB-`, `BB-→B+`, `B+→B`, `B→B-`, `B-→CCC+`, `CCC+→CCC`, `CCC→CCC-`),
- when `notchChange(S[i], S[i+1])` is called,
- then it returns `1`. The reverse `notchChange(S[i+1], S[i])` returns `-1`.

**AC-9 (C1; C3): extremes**
- Given the ends of the scale,
- when `notchChange('AAA','CCC-')` and `notchChange('CCC-','AAA')` are called,
- then they return `18` and `-18`.
- No pair of valid inputs gives a value outside `-18..18`.

### Trim and case (C1)

**AC-10 (C1): trimming**
- Given padded inputs,
- when they are passed to `notchChange`, then they behave exactly like the trimmed rating:

| Call | Expected |
|---|---|
| `notchChange(' BBB+ ', 'BB+')` | `3` |
| `notchChange('BB+', '\tBBB+\n')` | `-3` |
| `notchChange(' A ', 'A')` (NBSP, removed by `trim()`) | `0` |
| `notchChange('\r\n AAA', 'CCC- ﻿')` | `18` |

**AC-11 (C1): case-insensitivity**
- Given lower- or mixed-case inputs,
- when they are passed to `notchChange`, then they match the upper-case rating:

| Call | Expected |
|---|---|
| `notchChange('bbb+', 'BBB+')` | `0` |
| `notchChange('bbb+', 'bb+')` | `3` |
| `notchChange('Bb+', ' bBb+ ')` | `-3` |
| `notchChange('aaa', 'ccc-')` | `18` |
| `notchChange('aA-', 'AA-')` | `0` |

Trim and case-folding also apply to every rating in AC-7. For example, `notchChange(S[i].toLowerCase(), ' ' + S[j] + ' ')` returns `j - i`.

### Invalid input (C2; readiness CON-errors). Every value is checked in both argument positions

For each value `v` in the classes below, both `notchChange(v, 'A')` and `notchChange('A', v)` must throw a `RangeError`, checked with `assert.throws(fn, RangeError)`. Neither call may return a value, and neither may throw a `TypeError` or any other error type.

**AC-12 (C2): non-string primitives**
- Given `v` ∈ {`undefined`, `null`, `0`, `7`, `3.5`, `NaN`, `true`, `false`, `1n`, `Symbol('A')`},
- when called as above,
- then a `RangeError` is thrown.
- The missing-argument forms are covered too: `notchChange()` and `notchChange('A')` throw `RangeError`.

**AC-13 (C2): non-string objects, including String objects**
- Given `v` ∈ {`new String('A')`, `new String('BBB+')`, `['A']`, `[]`, `{}`, `{ toString() { return 'A'; } }`, `Object.create(null)`, `() => 'A'`, `new Date(0)`},
- when called as above,
- then a `RangeError` is thrown.
- `new String('A')` and `['A']` are not coerced, even though `String(v) === 'A'`.

**AC-14 (C2): empty and whitespace-only strings**
- Given `v` ∈ {`''`, `' '`, `'\t\n'`, `' '`},
- when called as above,
- then a `RangeError` is thrown.

**AC-15 (C2; C1): unknown ratings**
- Given `v` ∈ {`'CC'`, `'C'`, `'D'`, `'NR'`, `'SD'`, `'BBB++'`, `'AAAA'`, `'BBB +'` (internal space), `'B B'`, `'A−'` (Unicode minus), `'A＋'` (fullwidth plus), `'constructor'`, `'__proto__'`, `'toString'`},
- when called as above,
- then a `RangeError` is thrown.

**AC-16 (C2; X-error-message): both arguments invalid, and message safety**
- Given both arguments are invalid, e.g. `(Symbol('x'), 42)`, `(null, 'CC')`, `('', Symbol('y'))` and `(Object.create(null), new String('A'))`,
- when `notchChange` is called,
- then it throws a `RangeError`. Building the message must never raise a different error. In particular a Symbol or `Object.create(null)` in either position still gives a `RangeError`, not a `TypeError`.
- `previous` is validated before `current`, so the message names `previous`. The tests assert only the error type (X-error-message). The check order and the message wording (argument name, `typeof` for non-strings) are confirmed in code review.

### Purity (C4; CLAUDE.md)

**AC-17 (C4; CLAUDE.md): no imports, I/O or output**
- Given `src/ratings/notch.mjs`,
- when it is inspected with `grep -nE "^\s*import|require\(|console\.|process\." src/ratings/notch.mjs`,
- then nothing matches.
- Calling `notchChange` on valid and invalid inputs writes nothing to stdout or stderr. `package.json` gains no `dependencies` or `devDependencies`.

**AC-18 (readiness DEL-ci; TST-strategy): test run and file locations**
- Given the delivered card,
- when `npm test` runs from the repo root,
- then it exits 0. The run includes `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` and the QA tests under `test/integration/ratings/`, which together cover AC-1 to AC-16.

## Risks and assumptions

**Risks.** These are the likely mistakes, since the developer runs on the haiku model.
- Calling `.trim()` or `.toUpperCase()` before the type check. This turns non-strings into a `TypeError` (AC-12) or coerces `new String('A')` and `['A']` into valid ratings (AC-13). The check must be `typeof v === 'string'`.
- Building the message with `'…' + value` or a template literal. This throws a `TypeError` for Symbols and for `Object.create(null)` (AC-16).
- Looking ratings up in a plain object map. Prototype keys can then match (AC-15 `'constructor'`, `'__proto__'`). Looking up the index in the frozen array avoids this.
- Reversing the sign (`previous - current`). AC-4 and AC-5 catch it.
- Writing the scale with typographic minus or plus signs. AC-1 checks the code points.

**Assumptions.**
- The contract needs only the two named exports. It neither requires nor forbids a default export, so none is planned.
- Extra arguments beyond two are ignored. The request is silent on them and it does not change the result for valid calls.
- "Whitespace" means exactly what `String.prototype.trim()` removes (ECMAScript WhiteSpace and LineTerminator, including NBSP and BOM), as C1 states.
- The examples were checked against C1 (BBB+ = 7, BB+ = 10). With C3's sign they agree, so there is no contradiction (readiness PRD-conflicts).
- `RangeError` for non-strings, rather than the usual `TypeError`, is deliberate and binding (C2).

5	## Goal

Any invalid input throws a `RangeError`. Indicators 11, 12 and 13 and the full REQ-06-02 notch calculator will be built on this later (readiness PRD-goal). The work is done when every AC below passes under `npm test` (`node --test`) (readiness DEL-ci).
8	
9	## Scope
10	
11	- One card, one component: `ratings` (library, node). Code goes in `src/ratings/notch.mjs`. Developer unit tests go in `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`. QA's consumer-level tests go in `test/integration/ratings/` (readiness ARC-components, TST-strategy).
12	- `RATING_SCALE` is a frozen array of the 19 ratings in C1 order (readiness CON-interface, X-scale-immutability).
13	- `notchChange(previous, current)` returns `index(current) - index(previous)` after `String.prototype.trim()` and case-insensitive matching (REQ-06-02, C1, C3).

28	## Acceptance criteria
29	<!-- Each one must be testable. Cards reference these ids. -->
30	
31	Notation: `S` = the imported `RATING_SCALE`. Index 0 = `AAA` … index 18 = `CCC-`. Equality checks use `assert.strictEqual` (Object.is semantics).
32	
33	### Contract and scale
34	
35	**AC-1 (Contract; C1; X-scale-immutability): scale content and order**
36	- Given `import { RATING_SCALE } from './src/ratings/notch.mjs'`,
37	- when it is read,
38	- then `Array.isArray(RATING_SCALE) === true`, `RATING_SCALE.length === 19`, and `assert.deepStrictEqual(RATING_SCALE, ['AAA','AA+','AA','AA-','A+','A','A-','BBB+','BBB','BBB-','BB+','BB','BB-','B+','B','B-','CCC+','CCC','CCC-'])`. Every element is a primitive string with ASCII `+` (U+002B) and `-` (U+002D).
39	
40	**AC-2 (X-scale-immutability; C1): scale is frozen**
41	- Given the imported `RATING_SCALE`,
42	- when `Object.isFrozen(RATING_SCALE)` is checked and, in strict-mode test code, `RATING_SCALE.push('CC')`, `RATING_SCALE[0] = 'X'`, `RATING_SCALE.length = 0` and `RATING_SCALE.reverse()` are each tried,
43	- then `Object.isFrozen` returns `true` and each mutation throws `TypeError`.
44	- Afterwards `RATING_SCALE[0] === 'AAA'`, `RATING_SCALE.length === 19` and `notchChange('AAA','CCC-') === 18`.
45	
46	**AC-3 (Contract; C3; readiness ARC-async): return type**
47	- Given valid inputs `('BBB+','BB+')`,
48	- when `notchChange` is called,
49	- then the result is not a Promise, `typeof result === 'number'` and `Number.isInteger(result) === true`.
50	- For `('A','A')` the result is `+0`: `Object.is(result, 0) === true`, never `-0`.
51	
52	### REQ-06-02 examples
53	
54	**AC-4 (REQ-06-02; C3): downgrade.** Given `previous = 'BBB+'` and `current = 'BB+'`, when `notchChange('BBB+','BB+')` is called, then it returns `3`.
55	
56	**AC-5 (REQ-06-02; C3): upgrade.** Given `previous = 'BB+'` and `current = 'BBB+'`, when `notchChange('BB+','BBB+')` is called, then it returns `-3`.
57	
58	**AC-6 (REQ-06-02; C3): unchanged.** Given `previous = 'A'` and `current = 'A'`, when `notchChange('A','A')` is called, then it returns `0`.
59	
60	### Full scale (X-test-coverage)
61	
62	**AC-7 (C1; C3): every pair**
63	- Given every pair `(i, j)` with `i, j ∈ 0..18` (361 pairs),
64	- when `notchChange(S[i], S[j])` is called,
65	- then it returns `j - i`. This includes `0` for all 19 cases where `i === j`, and `notchChange(a,b) === -notchChange(b,a)` for every pair.
66	
67	**AC-8 (C1; C3): adjacent steps**
68	- Given each of the 18 adjacent pairs (`AAA→AA+`, `AA+→AA`, `AA→AA-`, `AA-→A+`, `A+→A`, `A→A-`, `A-→BBB+`, `BBB+→BBB`, `BBB→BBB-`, `BBB-→BB+`, `BB+→BB`, `BB→BB-`, `BB-→B+`, `B+→B`, `B→B-`, `B-→CCC+`, `CCC+→CCC`, `CCC→CCC-`),
69	- when `notchChange(S[i], S[i+1])` is called,
70	- then it returns `1`. The reverse `notchChange(S[i+1], S[i])` returns `-1`.
71	
72	**AC-9 (C1; C3): extremes**
73	- Given the ends of the scale,
74	- when `notchChange('AAA','CCC-')` and `notchChange('CCC-','AAA')` are called,
75	- then they return `18` and `-18`.
76	- No pair of valid inputs gives a value outside `-18..18`.
77	
78	### Trim and case (C1)
79	
80	**AC-10 (C1): trimming**
81	- Given padded inputs,
82	- when they are passed to `notchChange`, then they behave exactly like the trimmed rating:
83	
84	| Call | Expected |
85	|---|---|
86	| `notchChange(' BBB+ ', 'BB+')` | `3` |
87	| `notchChange('BB+', '\tBBB+\n')` | `-3` |
88	| `notchChange(' A ', 'A')` (NBSP, removed by `trim()`) | `0` |
89	| `notchChange('\r\n AAA', 'CCC- ﻿')` | `18` |
90	
91	**AC-11 (C1): case-insensitivity**
92	- Given lower- or mixed-case inputs,
93	- when they are passed to `notchChange`, then they match the upper-case rating:
94	
95	| Call | Expected |
96	|---|---|
97	| `notchChange('bbb+', 'BBB+')` | `0` |
98	| `notchChange('bbb+', 'bb+')` | `3` |
99	| `notchChange('Bb+', ' bBb+ ')` | `-3` |
100	| `notchChange('aaa', 'ccc-')` | `18` |
101	| `notchChange('aA-', 'AA-')` | `0` |
102	
103	Trim and case-folding also apply to every rating in AC-7. For example, `notchChange(S[i].toLowerCase(), ' ' + S[j] + ' ')` returns `j - i`.
104	
105	### Invalid input (C2; readiness CON-errors). Every value is checked in both argument positions
106	
107	For each value `v` in the classes below, both `notchChange(v, 'A')` and `notchChange('A', v)` must throw a `RangeError`, checked with `assert.throws(fn, RangeError)`. Neither call may return a value, and neither may throw a `TypeError` or any other error type.
108	
109	**AC-12 (C2): non-string primitives**
110	- Given `v` ∈ {`undefined`, `null`, `0`, `7`, `3.5`, `NaN`, `true`, `false`, `1n`, `Symbol('A')`},
111	- when called as above,
112	- then a `RangeError` is thrown.
113	- The missing-argument forms are covered too: `notchChange()` and `notchChange('A')` throw `RangeError`.
114	
115	**AC-13 (C2): non-string objects, including String objects**
116	- Given `v` ∈ {`new String('A')`, `new String('BBB+')`, `['A']`, `[]`, `{}`, `{ toString() { return 'A'; } }`, `Object.create(null)`, `() => 'A'`, `new Date(0)`},
117	- when called as above,
118	- then a `RangeError` is thrown.
119	- `new String('A')` and `['A']` are not coerced, even though `String(v) === 'A'`.
120	
121	**AC-14 (C2): empty and whitespace-only strings**
122	- Given `v` ∈ {`''`, `' '`, `'\t\n'`, `' '`},
123	- when called as above,
124	- then a `RangeError` is thrown.
125	
126	**AC-15 (C2; C1): unknown ratings**
127	- Given `v` ∈ {`'CC'`, `'C'`, `'D'`, `'NR'`, `'SD'`, `'BBB++'`, `'AAAA'`, `'BBB +'` (internal space), `'B B'`, `'A−'` (Unicode minus), `'A＋'` (fullwidth plus), `'constructor'`, `'__proto__'`, `'toString'`},
128	- when called as above,
129	- then a `RangeError` is thrown.
130	
131	**AC-16 (C2; X-error-message): both arguments invalid, and message safety**
132	- Given both arguments are invalid, e.g. `(Symbol('x'), 42)`, `(null, 'CC')`, `('', Symbol('y'))` and `(Object.create(null), new String('A'))`,
133	- when `notchChange` is called,
134	- then it throws a `RangeError`. Building the message must never raise a different error. In particular a Symbol or `Object.create(null)` in either position still gives a `RangeError`, not a `TypeError`.
135	- `previous` is validated before `current`, so the message names `previous`. The tests assert only the error type (X-error-message). The check order and the message wording (argument name, `typeof` for non-strings) are confirmed in code review.
136	
137	### Purity (C4; CLAUDE.md)
138	
139	**AC-17 (C4; CLAUDE.md): no imports, I/O or output**
140	- Given `src/ratings/notch.mjs`,
141	- when it is inspected with `grep -nE "^\s*import|require\(|console\.|process\." src/ratings/notch.mjs`,
142	- then nothing matches.
143	- Calling `notchChange` on valid and invalid inputs writes nothing to stdout or stderr. `package.json` gains no `dependencies` or `devDependencies`.
144	
145	**AC-18 (readiness DEL-ci; TST-strategy): test run and file locations**
146	- Given the delivered card,
147	- when `npm test` runs from the repo root,
148	- then it exits 0. The run includes `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` and the QA tests under `test/integration/ratings/`, which together cover AC-1 to AC-16.
149	
150	## Risks and assumptions
151	
152	**Risks.** These are the likely mistakes, since the developer runs on the haiku model.
153	- Calling `.trim()` or `.toUpperCase()` before the type check. This turns non-strings into a `TypeError` (AC-12) or coerces `new String('A')` and `['A']` into valid ratings (AC-13). The check must be `typeof v === 'string'`.
154	- Building the message with `'…' + value` or a template literal. This throws a `TypeError` for Symbols and for `Object.create(null)` (AC-16).
155	- Looking ratings up in a plain object map. Prototype keys can then match (AC-15 `'constructor'`, `'__proto__'`). Looking up the index in the frozen array avoids this.
156	- Reversing the sign (`previous - current`). AC-4 and AC-5 catch it.
157	- Writing the scale with typographic minus or plus signs. AC-1 checks the code points.
158	
159	**Assumptions.**
160	- The contract needs only the two named exports. It neither requires nor forbids a default export, so none is planned.
161	- Extra arguments beyond two are ignored. The request is silent on them and it does not change the result for valid calls.
162	- "Whitespace" means exactly what `String.prototype.trim()` removes (ECMAScript WhiteSpace and LineTerminator, including NBSP and BOM), as C1 states.
163	- The examples were checked against C1 (BBB+ = 7, BB+ = 10). With C3's sign they agree, so there is no contradiction (readiness PRD-conflicts).
164	- `RangeError` for non-strings, rather than the usual `TypeError`, is deliberate and binding (C2).

4	
5	## Goal
6	
7	Deliver the notch-change primitive for the Watchlist POC: a pure, synchronous ES module `src/ratings/notch.mjs` that exports `RATING_SCALE` (the 19 C1 ratings, best first, frozen) and `notchChange(previous, current)`. `notchChange` returns the signed number of steps from `previous` to `current`: downgrade is positive, upgrade is negative, unchanged is 0. Any invalid input throws a `RangeError`. Indicators 11, 12 and 13 and the full REQ-06-02 notch calculator will be built on this later (readiness PRD-goal). The work is done when every AC below passes under `npm test` (`node --test`) (readiness DEL-ci).
8	
9	## Scope
10	
11	- One card, one component: `ratings` (library, node). Code goes in `src/ratings/notch.mjs`. Developer unit tests go in `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`. QA's consumer-level tests go in `test/integration/ratings/` (readiness ARC-components, TST-strategy).
12	- `RATING_SCALE` is a frozen array of the 19 ratings in C1 order (readiness CON-interface, X-scale-immutability).
13	- `notchChange(previous, current)` returns `index(current) - index(previous)` after `String.prototype.trim()` and case-insensitive matching (REQ-06-02, C1, C3).
14	- Input validation: each argument is rejected with a `RangeError` for every C2 class. `previous` is validated before `current`, and the error message is built safely (C2, readiness CON-errors, X-error-message).
15	- Inline JSDoc on both exports covering the sign convention and the `RangeError` (readiness DEL-docs).
16	- Plain Node 18+ ESM. No dependencies, no imports, no I/O, no console output (CLAUDE.md, C4).
17	
18	## Out of scope
19	
20	- Indicators 11, 12 and 13, the rest of REQ-06-02 (the notch calculator itself), and every other POC requirement (readiness PRD-scope).
21	- Ratings outside the 19-step scale (CC, C, D, NR, SD, etc.). Callers get a `RangeError` for these; there is no mapping or fallback.
22	- Any UI, CLI, printed or logged output, persistence, rating sources or external systems (C4, readiness ARC-data, ARC-integration, NFR-observability).
23	- Converting non-primitive inputs: String objects, arrays and objects with `toString` are never coerced (C2).
24	- Asserting the exact text of the error message. Only the error type is asserted (X-error-message).
25	- README, changelog or runbook changes (readiness DEL-docs).
26	- Performance targets (readiness NFR-performance) and banking-regulation or internal-policy constraints (C2, readiness NFR-compliance).
27	
28	## Acceptance criteria
29	<!-- Each one must be testable. Cards reference these ids. -->
30	
31	Notation: `S` = the imported `RATING_SCALE`. Index 0 = `AAA` … index 18 = `CCC-`. Equality checks use `assert.strictEqual` (Object.is semantics).
32	
33	### Contract and scale
34	
35	**AC-1 (Contract; C1; X-scale-immutability): scale content and order**
36	- Given `import { RATING_SCALE } from './src/ratings/notch.mjs'`,
37	- when it is read,
38	- then `Array.isArray(RATING_SCALE) === true`, `RATING_SCALE.length === 19`, and `assert.deepStrictEqual(RATING_SCALE, ['AAA','AA+','AA','AA-','A+','A','A-','BBB+','BBB','BBB-','BB+','BB','BB-','B+','B','B-','CCC+','CCC','CCC-'])`. Every element is a primitive string with ASCII `+` (U+002B) and `-` (U+002D).
39	
40	**AC-2 (X-scale-immutability; C1): scale is frozen**
41	- Given the imported `RATING_SCALE`,
42	- when `Object.isFrozen(RATING_SCALE)` is checked and, in strict-mode test code, `RATING_SCALE.push('CC')`, `RATING_SCALE[0] = 'X'`, `RATING_SCALE.length = 0` and `RATING_SCALE.reverse()` are each tried,
43	- then `Object.isFrozen` returns `true` and each mutation throws `TypeError`.
44	- Afterwards `RATING_SCALE[0] === 'AAA'`, `RATING_SCALE.length === 19` and `notchChange('AAA','CCC-') === 18`.
45	
46	**AC-3 (Contract; C3; readiness ARC-async): return type**
47	- Given valid inputs `('BBB+','BB+')`,
48	- when `notchChange` is called,
49	- then the result is not a Promise, `typeof result === 'number'` and `Number.isInteger(result) === true`.
50	- For `('A','A')` the result is `+0`: `Object.is(result, 0) === true`, never `-0`.
51	
52	### REQ-06-02 examples
53	
54	**AC-4 (REQ-06-02; C3): downgrade.** Given `previous = 'BBB+'` and `current = 'BB+'`, when `notchChange('BBB+','BB+')` is called, then it returns `3`.
55	
56	**AC-5 (REQ-06-02; C3): upgrade.** Given `previous = 'BB+'` and `current = 'BBB+'`, when `notchChange('BB+','BBB+')` is called, then it returns `-3`.
57	
58	**AC-6 (REQ-06-02; C3): unchanged.** Given `previous = 'A'` and `current = 'A'`, when `notchChange('A','A')` is called, then it returns `0`.
59	
60	### Full scale (X-test-coverage)
61	
62	**AC-7 (C1; C3): every pair**
63	- Given every pair `(i, j)` with `i, j ∈ 0..18` (361 pairs),
64	- when `notchChange(S[i], S[j])` is called,
65	- then it returns `j - i`. This includes `0` for all 19 cases where `i === j`, and `notchChange(a,b) === -notchChange(b,a)` for every pair.
66	
67	**AC-8 (C1; C3): adjacent steps**
68	- Given each of the 18 adjacent pairs (`AAA→AA+`, `AA+→AA`, `AA→AA-`, `AA-→A+`, `A+→A`, `A→A-`, `A-→BBB+`, `BBB+→BBB`, `BBB→BBB-`, `BBB-→BB+`, `BB+→BB`, `BB→BB-`, `BB-→B+`, `B+→B`, `B→B-`, `B-→CCC+`, `CCC+→CCC`, `CCC→CCC-`),
69	- when `notchChange(S[i], S[i+1])` is called,
70	- then it returns `1`. The reverse `notchChange(S[i+1], S[i])` returns `-1`.
71	
72	**AC-9 (C1; C3): extremes**
73	- Given the ends of the scale,
74	- when `notchChange('AAA','CCC-')` and `notchChange('CCC-','AAA')` are called,
75	- then they return `18` and `-18`.
76	- No pair of valid inputs gives a value outside `-18..18`.
77	
78	### Trim and case (C1)
79	
80	**AC-10 (C1): trimming**
81	- Given padded inputs,
82	- when they are passed to `notchChange`, then they behave exactly like the trimmed rating:
83	
84	| Call | Expected |
85	|---|---|
86	| `notchChange(' BBB+ ', 'BB+')` | `3` |
87	| `notchChange('BB+', '\tBBB+\n')` | `-3` |
88	| `notchChange(' A ', 'A')` (NBSP, removed by `trim()`) | `0` |
89	| `notchChange('\r\n AAA', 'CCC- ﻿')` | `18` |
90	
91	**AC-11 (C1): case-insensitivity**
92	- Given lower- or mixed-case inputs,
93	- when they are passed to `notchChange`, then they match the upper-case rating:
94	
95	| Call | Expected |
96	|---|---|
97	| `notchChange('bbb+', 'BBB+')` | `0` |
98	| `notchChange('bbb+', 'bb+')` | `3` |
99	| `notchChange('Bb+', ' bBb+ ')` | `-3` |
100	| `notchChange('aaa', 'ccc-')` | `18` |
101	| `notchChange('aA-', 'AA-')` | `0` |
102	
103	Trim and case-folding also apply to every rating in AC-7. For example, `notchChange(S[i].toLowerCase(), ' ' + S[j] + ' ')` returns `j - i`.
104	
105	### Invalid input (C2; readiness CON-errors). Every value is checked in both argument positions
106	
107	For each value `v` in the classes below, both `notchChange(v, 'A')` and `notchChange('A', v)` must throw a `RangeError`, checked with `assert.throws(fn, RangeError)`. Neither call may return a value, and neither may throw a `TypeError` or any other error type.
108	
109	**AC-12 (C2): non-string primitives**
110	- Given `v` ∈ {`undefined`, `null`, `0`, `7`, `3.5`, `NaN`, `true`, `false`, `1n`, `Symbol('A')`},
111	- when called as above,
112	- then a `RangeError` is thrown.
113	- The missing-argument forms are covered too: `notchChange()` and `notchChange('A')` throw `RangeError`.
114	
115	**AC-13 (C2): non-string objects, including String objects**
116	- Given `v` ∈ {`new String('A')`, `new String('BBB+')`, `['A']`, `[]`, `{}`, `{ toString() { return 'A'; } }`, `Object.create(null)`, `() => 'A'`, `new Date(0)`},
117	- when called as above,
118	- then a `RangeError` is thrown.
119	- `new String('A')` and `['A']` are not coerced, even though `String(v) === 'A'`.
120	
121	**AC-14 (C2): empty and whitespace-only strings**
122	- Given `v` ∈ {`''`, `' '`, `'\t\n'`, `' '`},
123	- when called as above,
124	- then a `RangeError` is thrown.
125	
126	**AC-15 (C2; C1): unknown ratings**
127	- Given `v` ∈ {`'CC'`, `'C'`, `'D'`, `'NR'`, `'SD'`, `'BBB++'`, `'AAAA'`, `'BBB +'` (internal space), `'B B'`, `'A−'` (Unicode minus), `'A＋'` (fullwidth plus), `'constructor'`, `'__proto__'`, `'toString'`},
128	- when called as above,
129	- then a `RangeError` is thrown.
130	
131	**AC-16 (C2; X-error-message): both arguments invalid, and message safety**
132	- Given both arguments are invalid, e.g. `(Symbol('x'), 42)`, `(null, 'CC')`, `('', Symbol('y'))` and `(Object.create(null), new String('A'))`,
133	- when `notchChange` is called,
134	- then it throws a `RangeError`. Building the message must never raise a different error. In particular a Symbol or `Object.create(null)` in either position still gives a `RangeError`, not a `TypeError`.
135	- `previous` is validated before `current`, so the message names `previous`. The tests assert only the error type (X-error-message). The check order and the message wording (argument name, `typeof` for non-strings) are confirmed in code review.
136	
137	### Purity (C4; CLAUDE.md)
138	
139	**AC-17 (C4; CLAUDE.md): no imports, I/O or output**
140	- Given `src/ratings/notch.mjs`,
141	- when it is inspected with `grep -nE "^\s*import|require\(|console\.|process\." src/ratings/notch.mjs`,
142	- then nothing matches.
143	- Calling `notchChange` on valid and invalid inputs writes nothing to stdout or stderr. `package.json` gains no `dependencies` or `devDependencies`.
144	
145	**AC-18 (readiness DEL-ci; TST-strategy): test run and file locations**
146	- Given the delivered card,
147	- when `npm test` runs from the repo root,
148	- then it exits 0. The run includes `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` and the QA tests under `test/integration/ratings/`, which together cover AC-1 to AC-16.
149	
150	## Risks and assumptions
151	
152	**Risks.** These are the likely mistakes, since the developer runs on the haiku model.
153	- Calling `.trim()` or `.toUpperCase()` before the type check. This turns non-strings into a `TypeError` (AC-12) or coerces `new String('A')` and `['A']` into valid ratings (AC-13). The check must be `typeof v === 'string'`.
154	- Building the message with `'…' + value` or a template literal. This throws a `TypeError` for Symbols and for `Object.create(null)` (AC-16).
155	- Looking ratings up in a plain object map. Prototype keys can then match (AC-15 `'constructor'`, `'__proto__'`). Looking up the index in the frozen array avoids this.
156	- Reversing the sign (`previous - current`). AC-4 and AC-5 catch it.
157	- Writing the scale with typographic minus or plus signs. AC-1 checks the code points.
158	
159	**Assumptions.**
160	- The contract needs only the two named exports. It neither requires nor forbids a default export, so none is planned.
161	- Extra arguments beyond two are ignored. The request is silent on them and it does not change the result for valid calls.
162	- "Whitespace" means exactly what `String.prototype.trim()` removes (ECMAScript WhiteSpace and LineTerminator, including NBSP and BOM), as C1 states.
163	- The examples were checked against C1 (BBB+ = 7, BB+ = 10). With C3's sign they agree, so there is no contradiction (readiness PRD-conflicts).
164	- `RangeError` for non-strings, rather than the usual `TypeError`, is deliberate and binding (C2).
165	
166	## Open questions
167	<!-- Questions whose answers would change the scope. Asked to the human at plan approval. -->
168	
169	None. All 30 readiness items are decided or not applicable. The three PM decisions (X-scale-immutability, X-error-message, X-test-coverage) are applied above and do not change scope.

=== T-01 ===
# T-01: ratings: add RATING_SCALE and notchChange(previous, current) in src/ratings/notch.mjs, with unit tests

## User story
As a developer building Watchlist indicators 11–13 and the REQ-06-02 notch calculator, I want one pure function that gives the signed number of notches between two credit ratings on the 19-step scale, so that every later consumer uses the same scale, sign convention and validation.

## Traces to
AC-1 to AC-18 (plan.md). REQ-06-02. Clarifications C1 (scale, trim, case), C2 (RangeError for every invalid class), C3 (sign, integer), C4 (pure). Readiness CON-interface, CON-errors, ARC-async, DEL-docs, DEL-ci, TST-strategy, X-scale-immutability, X-error-message, X-test-coverage. CLAUDE.md.

## What to build
| File | Owner | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `src/ratings/notch.mjs` (new) | backend dev | Two named exports and no default export: `RATING_SCALE` and `notchChange(previous, current)`. It may have a private helper such as `indexOfRating(value, argName)`. JSDoc goes on both exports. |
| `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` (new) | backend dev | `node:test` + `node:assert/strict` unit tests for AC-1 to AC-16. |
| `test/integration/ratings/*.test.mjs` | QA only | Consumer-level tests. The dev does not create files here. |

- `RATING_SCALE` is `Object.freeze([...])` holding the 19 C1 ratings, best first. Index 0 is `'AAA'`, 7 is `'BBB+'`, 10 is `'BB+'` and 18 is `'CCC-'`. Every sign is ASCII U+002B / U+002D.
- `notchChange(previous, current)` is synchronous and returns `index(current) - index(previous)`, an integer in -18..18.
- Validation order for each argument, `previous` first:
  1. `typeof v === 'string'`, else `RangeError`.
  2. `v.trim().toUpperCase()`.
  3. `RATING_SCALE.indexOf(key)`. If the result is -1, throw `RangeError`.
- The error message names the argument. It uses `typeof v` for non-strings and `JSON.stringify(v)` for unknown strings. The raw value is never concatenated or interpolated (X-error-message).
- JSDoc on `RATING_SCALE`:
  - it holds the 19 ratings, best first
  - it is frozen
  - the index is the notch position
- JSDoc on `notchChange`:
  - `@param {string} previous`, `@param {string} current`, `@returns {number}`
  - the sign convention: positive = downgrade, negative = upgrade, 0 = unchanged, range -18..18
  - trim and case-insensitive matching
  - `@throws {RangeError}` for non-strings (including String objects), empty or whitespace-only strings and unknown ratings, with `previous` checked first

## Acceptance criteria
1. **AC-1**: Given `import { RATING_SCALE } from '../../src/ratings/notch.mjs'`, when it is read, then:
   - `Array.isArray(RATING_SCALE) === true` and `RATING_SCALE.length === 19`
   - `assert.deepStrictEqual(RATING_SCALE, ['AAA','AA+','AA','AA-','A+','A','A-','BBB+','BBB','BBB-','BB+','BB','BB-','B+','B','B-','CCC+','CCC','CCC-'])` passes
   - every element has `typeof === 'string'` and matches `/^[ABC]{1,3}[+-]?$/` (ASCII `+` U+002B and `-` U+002D only)
2. **AC-2**: Given `RATING_SCALE`, then:
   - `Object.isFrozen(RATING_SCALE) === true`
   - in strict mode, `RATING_SCALE.push('CC')`, `RATING_SCALE[0] = 'X'`, `RATING_SCALE.length = 0` and `RATING_SCALE.reverse()` each throw `TypeError`
   - afterwards `RATING_SCALE[0] === 'AAA'`, `RATING_SCALE.length === 19` and `notchChange('AAA','CCC-') === 18`
3. **AC-3**: Given `('BBB+','BB+')`, when `notchChange` is called, then:
   - `result instanceof Promise === false`, `typeof result === 'number'` and `Number.isInteger(result) === true`
   - `Object.is(notchChange('A','A'), 0) === true` (+0, never -0)
4. **AC-4**: Given `('BBB+','BB+')`, when `notchChange` is called, then it returns `3`. This is a downgrade.
5. **AC-5**: Given `('BB+','BBB+')`, when `notchChange` is called, then it returns `-3`. This is an upgrade.
6. **AC-6**: Given `('A','A')`, when `notchChange` is called, then it returns `0`. This is unchanged.
7. **AC-7**: Given all 361 pairs `(i, j)` with `i, j ∈ 0..18`, when `notchChange(S[i], S[j])` is called, then:
   - it returns `j - i`, which is 0 for the 19 cases where `i === j`
   - `notchChange(S[i],S[j]) === -notchChange(S[j],S[i])`
8. **AC-8**: Given the 18 adjacent pairs (`AAA→AA+` … `CCC→CCC-`), then `notchChange(S[i],S[i+1]) === 1` and `notchChange(S[i+1],S[i]) === -1`.
9. **AC-9**: Given the ends of the scale, then:
   - `notchChange('AAA','CCC-') === 18` and `notchChange('CCC-','AAA') === -18`
   - no valid pair from AC-7 returns a value outside `-18..18`
10. **AC-10**: Given padded inputs, then they behave like the trimmed rating:
    - `(' BBB+ ','BB+')` returns `3`
    - `('BB+','\tBBB+\n')` returns `-3`
    - `('\u00A0A\u00A0','A')` returns `0`
    - `('\r\n AAA','CCC-\u00A0\uFEFF')` returns `18`
11. **AC-11**: Given lower- or mixed-case inputs, then:
    - `('bbb+','BBB+')` returns `0`, `('bbb+','bb+')` returns `3` and `('Bb+',' bBb+ ')` returns `-3`
    - `('aaa','ccc-')` returns `18` and `('aA-','AA-')` returns `0`
    - for all 361 pairs, `notchChange(S[i].toLowerCase(), ' ' + S[j] + ' ') === j - i`
12. **AC-12**: Given `v ∈ {undefined, null, 0, 7, 3.5, NaN, true, false, 1n, Symbol('A')}`, then:
    - `notchChange(v,'A')` and `notchChange('A',v)` each throw `RangeError`, checked with `assert.throws(fn, RangeError)`
    - `notchChange()` and `notchChange('A')` also throw `RangeError`
13. **AC-13**: Given `v ∈ {new String('A'), new String('BBB+'), ['A'], [], {}, { toString() { return 'A'; } }, Object.create(null), () => 'A', new Date(0)}`, then each throws `RangeError` in both positions. Nothing is coerced, even when `String(v) === 'A'`.
14. **AC-14**: Given `v ∈ {'', ' ', '\t\n', '\u00A0'}`, then each throws `RangeError` in both positions.
15. **AC-15**: Given `v ∈ {'CC','C','D','NR','SD','BBB++','AAAA','BBB +','B B','A\u2212','A\uFF0B','constructor','__proto__','toString'}`, then each throws `RangeError` in both positions.
16. **AC-16**: Given `(Symbol('x'), 42)`, `(null, 'CC')`, `('', Symbol('y'))` and `(Object.create(null), new String('A'))`, when `notchChange` is called, then each throws `RangeError` and never `TypeError`.
    - Code review confirms three things: `previous` is validated first, the message names the argument and uses `typeof` for non-strings, and there is no `'…' + v`, `${v}` or `String(v)`.
    - Tests assert only the error type.
17. **AC-17**: Given `src/ratings/notch.mjs`, then:
    - `grep -nE "^\s*import|require\(|console\.|process\." src/ratings/notch.mjs` prints nothing. This includes comments and JSDoc.
    - calls with valid and invalid inputs write nothing to stdout or stderr
    - `git diff main -- package.json` is empty (no `dependencies` or `devDependencies`)
18. **AC-18**: Given the delivered card plus QA's tests, when `npm test` runs from the card's checkout root, then:
    - it exits 0
    - TAP output lists `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` and the files under `test/integration/ratings/`, which together cover AC-1 to AC-16
    - `node --test test/ratings/*.test.mjs` (dev) and `node --test test/integration/ratings/*.test.mjs` (QA) each exit 0

## Edge cases
- **Type check before string methods.** `.trim()` or `.toUpperCase()` on a non-string would throw `TypeError` (fails AC-12). Coercion would make `new String('A')` or `['A']` valid (fails AC-13). Only `typeof v === 'string'` passes; `instanceof String`, `String(v)` and `v + ''` are not used.
- **Unsafe message building.** Concatenating or interpolating a Symbol or `Object.create(null)` throws `TypeError` and hides the `RangeError` (AC-12, AC-13, AC-16).
- **Lookup must use the array.** Use `RATING_SCALE.indexOf`. A plain object map or the `in` operator lets `'constructor'`, `'__proto__'` and `'toString'` match (AC-15).
- **Whitespace means `String.prototype.trim()` and nothing else.** NBSP and BOM are removed. Internal whitespace is not removed, so `'BBB +'` and `'B B'` are invalid.
- **Sign.** The result is `c - p`. `p - c` fails AC-4 and AC-5. Equal indexes give +0.
- **Missing or extra arguments.** A missing argument is `undefined` and throws `RangeError`. Arguments beyond two are ignored, for example `notchChange('A','A','x') === 0`.
- **Look-alike characters.** The Unicode minus U+2212, an en dash and the fullwidth plus U+FF0B are invalid, both in input and in the scale literal.
- **Both arguments invalid.** The error is raised for `previous` (AC-16).
- **Test discovery.** With no arguments, `npm test` (`node --test`) also finds `*.test.mjs` under `.work/` when it is run from the main checkout. AC-18 is therefore judged from the card's or job's checkout root.

## Test data

**Valid examples**
| previous | current | expected |
|---|---|---|
| `'BBB+'` | `'BB+'` | `3` |
| `'BB+'` | `'BBB+'` | `-3` |
| `'A'` | `'A'` | `0` (`Object.is` +0) |
| `'AAA'` | `'CCC-'` | `18` |
| `'CCC-'` | `'AAA'` | `-18` |
| `'AAA'` | `'AA+'` | `1` |
| `'CCC'` | `'CCC-'` | `1` |
| `'A-'` | `'BBB+'` | `1` |
| `'B-'` | `'CCC+'` | `1` |
| `S[i]` | `S[j]` | `j - i` (all 361) |

**Trim and case**
| previous | current | expected |
|---|---|---|
| `' BBB+ '` | `'BB+'` | `3` |
| `'BB+'` | `'\tBBB+\n'` | `-3` |
| `'\u00A0A\u00A0'` | `'A'` | `0` |
| `'\r\n AAA'` | `'CCC-\u00A0\uFEFF'` | `18` |
| `'bbb+'` | `'BBB+'` | `0` |
| `'bbb+'` | `'bb+'` | `3` |
| `'Bb+'` | `' bBb+ '` | `-3` |
| `'aaa'` | `'ccc-'` | `18` |
| `'aA-'` | `'AA-'` | `0` |
| `S[i].toLowerCase()` | `' ' + S[j] + ' '` | `j - i` |

**Invalid classes** (each `v` is tried as `(v,'A')` and as `('A',v)`, and both must throw `RangeError`)
| Class (AC) | Values |
|---|---|
| Non-string primitives (AC-12) | `undefined`, `null`, `0`, `7`, `3.5`, `NaN`, `true`, `false`, `1n`, `Symbol('A')`. Also the calls `notchChange()` and `notchChange('A')`. |
| Objects (AC-13) | `new String('A')`, `new String('BBB+')`, `['A']`, `[]`, `{}`, `{ toString() { return 'A'; } }`, `Object.create(null)`, `() => 'A'`, `new Date(0)` |
| Empty or whitespace (AC-14) | `''`, `' '`, `'\t\n'`, `'\u00A0'` |
| Unknown ratings (AC-15) | `'CC'`, `'C'`, `'D'`, `'NR'`, `'SD'`, `'BBB++'`, `'AAAA'`, `'BBB +'`, `'B B'`, `'A\u2212'`, `'A\uFF0B'`, `'constructor'`, `'__proto__'`, `'toString'` |
| Both invalid (AC-16) | `(Symbol('x'), 42)`, `(null, 'CC')`, `('', Symbol('y'))`, `(Object.create(null), new String('A'))` |

## Out of scope for this card
- Indicators 11, 12 and 13, the REQ-06-02 notch calculator itself, and every other POC requirement.
- Ratings outside the 19-step scale (CC, C, D, NR, SD and others). They throw, with no mapping or fallback.
- Coercing String objects, arrays or objects that have `toString`.
- Asserting the exact text of the error message. Only the type is tested; the wording is checked in review.
- A default export, and any export other than `RATING_SCALE` and `notchChange`.
- UI, CLI, logging, persistence, I/O and external rating sources.
- Changes to `package.json`, README, the changelog or runbooks, and new dependencies.
- Performance targets and regulatory or internal-policy rules.
- Dev-created files under `test/integration/ratings/`, which belong to QA. Any file outside `src/ratings/notch.mjs` and `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`.

I only read files and changed nothing. The spec is based on these:
- /tmp/claude-0/live/k050c/models/repo/.work/JOB-20261006-0115-rating-notch-change/plan.md

## User story
As a developer building Watchlist indicators 11–13 and the REQ-06-02 notch calculator, I want one pure function that gives the signed number of notches between two credit ratings on the 19-step scale, so that every later consumer uses the same scale, sign convention and validation.

## Traces to
AC-1 to AC-18 (plan.md). REQ-06-02. Clarifications C1 (scale, trim, case), C2 (RangeError for every invalid class), C3 (sign, integer), C4 (pure). Readiness CON-interface, CON-errors, ARC-async, DEL-docs, DEL-ci, TST-strategy, X-scale-immutability, X-error-message, X-test-coverage. CLAUDE.md.

## What to build
| File | Owner | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `src/ratings/notch.mjs` (new) | backend dev | Two named exports and no default export: `RATING_SCALE` and `notchChange(previous, current)`. It may have a private helper such as `indexOfRating(value, argName)`. JSDoc goes on both exports. |
| `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` (new) | backend dev | `node:test` + `node:assert/strict` unit tests for AC-1 to AC-16. |
| `test/integration/ratings/*.test.mjs` | QA only | Consumer-level tests. The dev does not create files here. |

- `RATING_SCALE` is `Object.freeze([...])` holding the 19 C1 ratings, best first. Index 0 is `'AAA'`, 7 is `'BBB+'`, 10 is `'BB+'` and 18 is `'CCC-'`. Every sign is ASCII U+002B / U+002D.
- `notchChange(previous, current)` is synchronous and returns `index(current) - index(previous)`, an integer in -18..18.
- Validation order for each argument, `previous` first:
  1. `typeof v === 'string'`, else `RangeError`.
  2. `v.trim().toUpperCase()`.
  3. `RATING_SCALE.indexOf(key)`. If the result is -1, throw `RangeError`.
- The error message names the argument. It uses `typeof v` for non-strings and `JSON.stringify(v)` for unknown strings. The raw value is never concatenated or interpolated (X-error-message).
- JSDoc on `RATING_SCALE`:
  - it holds the 19 ratings, best first
  - it is frozen
  - the index is the notch position
- JSDoc on `notchChange`:
  - `@param {string} previous`, `@param {string} current`, `@returns {number}`
  - the sign convention: positive = downgrade, negative = upgrade, 0 = unchanged, range -18..18
  - trim and case-insensitive matching
  - `@throws {RangeError}` for non-strings (including String objects), empty or whitespace-only strings and unknown ratings, with `previous` checked first

2. **AC-2**: Given `RATING_SCALE`, then:
   - `Object.isFrozen(RATING_SCALE) === true`

   - afterwards `RATING_SCALE[0] === 'AAA'`, `RATING_SCALE.length === 19` and `notchChange('AAA','CCC-') === 18`

   - `result instanceof Promise === false`, `typeof result === 'number'` and `Number.isInteger(result) === true`

   - `notchChange(S[i],S[j]) === -notchChange(S[j],S[i])`
8. **AC-8**: Given the 18 adjacent pairs (`AAA→AA+` … `CCC→CCC-`), then `notchChange(S[i],S[i+1]) === 1` and `notchChange(S[i+1],S[i]) === -1`.
9. **AC-9**: Given the ends of the scale, then:
   - `notchChange('AAA','CCC-') === 18` and `notchChange('CCC-','AAA') === -18`
   - no valid pair from AC-7 returns a value outside `-18..18`
10. **AC-10**: Given padded inputs, then they behave like the trimmed rating:
    - `(' BBB+ ','BB+')` returns `3`
    - `('BB+','\tBBB+\n')` returns `-3`
    - `(' A ','A')` returns `0`
    - `('\r\n AAA','CCC- ﻿')` returns `18`
11. **AC-11**: Given lower- or mixed-case inputs, then:
    - `('bbb+','BBB+')` returns `0`, `('bbb+','bb+')` returns `3` and `('Bb+',' bBb+ ')` returns `-3`
    - `('aaa','ccc-')` returns `18` and `('aA-','AA-')` returns `0`
    - for all 361 pairs, `notchChange(S[i].toLowerCase(), ' ' + S[j] + ' ') === j - i`
12. **AC-12**: Given `v ∈ {undefined, null, 0, 7, 3.5, NaN, true, false, 1n, Symbol('A')}`, then:
    - `notchChange(v,'A')` and `notchChange('A',v)` each throw `RangeError`, checked with `assert.throws(fn, RangeError)`
    - `notchChange()` and `notchChange('A')` also throw `RangeError`

15. **AC-15**: Given `v ∈ {'CC','C','D','NR','SD','BBB++','AAAA','BBB +','B B','A−','A＋','constructor','__proto__','toString'}`, then each throws `RangeError` in both positions.
16. **AC-16**: Given `(Symbol('x'), 42)`, `(null, 'CC')`, `('', Symbol('y'))` and `(Object.create(null), new String('A'))`, when `notchChange` is called, then each throws `RangeError` and never `TypeError`.
    - Code review confirms three things: `previous` is validated first, the message names the argument and uses `typeof` for non-strings, and there is no `'…' + v`, `${v}` or `String(v)`.
    - Tests assert only the error type.
17. **AC-17**: Given `src/ratings/notch.mjs`, then:
    - `grep -nE "^\s*import|require\(|console\.|process\." src/ratings/notch.mjs` prints nothing. This includes comments and JSDoc.
    - calls with valid and invalid inputs write nothing to stdout or stderr
    - `git diff main -- package.json` is empty (no `dependencies` or `devDependencies`)
18. **AC-18**: Given the delivered card plus QA's tests, when `npm test` runs from the card's checkout root, then:
    - it exits 0
    - TAP output lists `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` and the files under `test/integration/ratings/`, which together cover AC-1 to AC-16
    - `node --test test/ratings/*.test.mjs` (dev) and `node --test test/integration/ratings/*.test.mjs` (QA) each exit 0

## Edge cases
- **Type check before string methods.** `.trim()` or `.toUpperCase()` on a non-string would throw `TypeError` (fails AC-12). Coercion would make `new String('A')` or `['A']` valid (fails AC-13). Only `typeof v === 'string'` passes; `instanceof String`, `String(v)` and `v + ''` are not used.
- **Unsafe message building.** Concatenating or interpolating a Symbol or `Object.create(null)` throws `TypeError` and hides the `RangeError` (AC-12, AC-13, AC-16).
- **Lookup must use the array.** Use `RATING_SCALE.indexOf`. A plain object map or the `in` operator lets `'constructor'`, `'__proto__'` and `'toString'` match (AC-15).

# T-01: ratings: add RATING_SCALE and notchChange(previous, current) in src/ratings/notch.mjs, with unit tests

## User story
As a developer building Watchlist indicators 11–13 and the REQ-06-02 notch calculator, I want one pure function that gives the signed number of notches between two credit ratings on the 19-step scale, so that every later consumer uses the same scale, sign convention and validation.

## Traces to
AC-1 to AC-18 (plan.md). REQ-06-02. Clarifications C1 (scale, trim, case), C2 (RangeError for every invalid class), C3 (sign, integer), C4 (pure). Readiness CON-interface, CON-errors, ARC-async, DEL-docs, DEL-ci, TST-strategy, X-scale-immutability, X-error-message, X-test-coverage. CLAUDE.md.

## What to build
| File | Owner | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `src/ratings/notch.mjs` (new) | backend dev | Two named exports and no default export: `RATING_SCALE` and `notchChange(previous, current)`. It may have a private helper such as `indexOfRating(value, argName)`. JSDoc goes on both exports. |
| `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` (new) | backend dev | `node:test` + `node:assert/strict` unit tests for AC-1 to AC-16. |
| `test/integration/ratings/*.test.mjs` | QA only | Consumer-level tests. The dev does not create files here. |

- `RATING_SCALE` is `Object.freeze([...])` holding the 19 C1 ratings, best first. Index 0 is `'AAA'`, 7 is `'BBB+'`, 10 is `'BB+'` and 18 is `'CCC-'`. Every sign is ASCII U+002B / U+002D.
- `notchChange(previous, current)` is synchronous and returns `index(current) - index(previous)`, an integer in -18..18.
- Validation order for each argument, `previous` first:
  1. `typeof v === 'string'`, else `RangeError`.
  2. `v.trim().toUpperCase()`.
  3. `RATING_SCALE.indexOf(key)`. If the result is -1, throw `RangeError`.
- The error message names the argument. It uses `typeof v` for non-strings and `JSON.stringify(v)` for unknown strings. The raw value is never concatenated or interpolated (X-error-message).
- JSDoc on `RATING_SCALE`:
  - it holds the 19 ratings, best first
  - it is frozen
  - the index is the notch position
- JSDoc on `notchChange`:
  - `@param {string} previous`, `@param {string} current`, `@returns {number}`
  - the sign convention: positive = downgrade, negative = upgrade, 0 = unchanged, range -18..18
  - trim and case-insensitive matching
  - `@throws {RangeError}` for non-strings (including String objects), empty or whitespace-only strings and unknown ratings, with `previous` checked first

## Acceptance criteria
1. **AC-1**: Given `import { RATING_SCALE } from '../../src/ratings/notch.mjs'`, when it is read, then:
   - `Array.isArray(RATING_SCALE) === true` and `RATING_SCALE.length === 19`
   - `assert.deepStrictEqual(RATING_SCALE, ['AAA','AA+','AA','AA-','A+','A','A-','BBB+','BBB','BBB-','BB+','BB','BB-','B+','B','B-','CCC+','CCC','CCC-'])` passes
   - every element has `typeof === 'string'` and matches `/^[ABC]{1,3}[+-]?$/` (ASCII `+` U+002B and `-` U+002D only)
2. **AC-2**: Given `RATING_SCALE`, then:
   - `Object.isFrozen(RATING_SCALE) === true`
   - in strict mode, `RATING_SCALE.push('CC')`, `RATING_SCALE[0] = 'X'`, `RATING_SCALE.length = 0` and `RATING_SCALE.reverse()` each throw `TypeError`
   - afterwards `RATING_SCALE[0] === 'AAA'`, `RATING_SCALE.length === 19` and `notchChange('AAA','CCC-') === 18`
3. **AC-3**: Given `('BBB+','BB+')`, when `notchChange` is called, then:
   - `result instanceof Promise === false`, `typeof result === 'number'` and `Number.isInteger(result) === true`
   - `Object.is(notchChange('A','A'), 0) === true` (+0, never -0)
4. **AC-4**: Given `('BBB+','BB+')`, when `notchChange` is called, then it returns `3`. This is a downgrade.
5. **AC-5**: Given `('BB+','BBB+')`, when `notchChange` is called, then it returns `-3`. This is an upgrade.
6. **AC-6**: Given `('A','A')`, when `notchChange` is called, then it returns `0`. This is unchanged.
7. **AC-7**: Given all 361 pairs `(i, j)` with `i, j ∈ 0..18`, when `notchChange(S[i], S[j])` is called, then:
   - it returns `j - i`, which is 0 for the 19 cases where `i === j`
   - `notchChange(S[i],S[j]) === -notchChange(S[j],S[i])`
8. **AC-8**: Given the 18 adjacent pairs (`AAA→AA+` … `CCC→CCC-`), then `notchChange(S[i],S[i+1]) === 1` and `notchChange(S[i+1],S[i]) === -1`.
9. **AC-9**: Given the ends of the scale, then:
   - `notchChange('AAA','CCC-') === 18` and `notchChange('CCC-','AAA') === -18`
   - no valid pair from AC-7 returns a value outside `-18..18`
10. **AC-10**: Given padded inputs, then they behave like the trimmed rating:
    - `(' BBB+ ','BB+')` returns `3`
    - `('BB+','\tBBB+\n')` returns `-3`
    - `(' A ','A')` returns `0`
    - `('\r\n AAA','CCC- ﻿')` returns `18`
11. **AC-11**: Given lower- or mixed-case inputs, then:
    - `('bbb+','BBB+')` returns `0`, `('bbb+','bb+')` returns `3` and `('Bb+',' bBb+ ')` returns `-3`
    - `('aaa','ccc-')` returns `18` and `('aA-','AA-')` returns `0`
    - for all 361 pairs, `notchChange(S[i].toLowerCase(), ' ' + S[j] + ' ') === j - i`
12. **AC-12**: Given `v ∈ {undefined, null, 0, 7, 3.5, NaN, true, false, 1n, Symbol('A')}`, then:
    - `notchChange(v,'A')` and `notchChange('A',v)` each throw `RangeError`, checked with `assert.throws(fn, RangeError)`
    - `notchChange()` and `notchChange('A')` also throw `RangeError`
13. **AC-13**: Given `v ∈ {new String('A'), new String('BBB+'), ['A'], [], {}, { toString() { return 'A'; } }, Object.create(null), () => 'A', new Date(0)}`, then each throws `RangeError` in both positions. Nothing is coerced, even when `String(v) === 'A'`.
14. **AC-14**: Given `v ∈ {'', ' ', '\t\n', ' '}`, then each throws `RangeError` in both positions.
15. **AC-15**: Given `v ∈ {'CC','C','D','NR','SD','BBB++','AAAA','BBB +','B B','A−','A＋','constructor','__proto__','toString'}`, then each throws `RangeError` in both positions.
16. **AC-16**: Given `(Symbol('x'), 42)`, `(null, 'CC')`, `('', Symbol('y'))` and `(Object.create(null), new String('A'))`, when `notchChange` is called, then each throws `RangeError` and never `TypeError`.
    - Code review confirms three things: `previous` is validated first, the message names the argument and uses `typeof` for non-strings, and there is no `'…' + v`, `${v}` or `String(v)`.
    - Tests assert only the error type.
17. **AC-17**: Given `src/ratings/notch.mjs`, then:
    - `grep -nE "^\s*import|require\(|console\.|process\." src/ratings/notch.mjs` prints nothing. This includes comments and JSDoc.
    - calls with valid and invalid inputs write nothing to stdout or stderr
    - `git diff main -- package.json` is empty (no `dependencies` or `devDependencies`)
18. **AC-18**: Given the delivered card plus QA's tests, when `npm test` runs from the card's checkout root, then:
    - it exits 0
    - TAP output lists `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` and the files under `test/integration/ratings/`, which together cover AC-1 to AC-16
    - `node --test test/ratings/*.test.mjs` (dev) and `node --test test/integration/ratings/*.test.mjs` (QA) each exit 0

## Edge cases
- **Type check before string methods.** `.trim()` or `.toUpperCase()` on a non-string would throw `TypeError` (fails AC-12). Coercion would make `new String('A')` or `['A']` valid (fails AC-13). Only `typeof v === 'string'` passes; `instanceof String`, `String(v)` and `v + ''` are not used.
- **Unsafe message building.** Concatenating or interpolating a Symbol or `Object.create(null)` throws `TypeError` and hides the `RangeError` (AC-12, AC-13, AC-16).
- **Lookup must use the array.** Use `RATING_SCALE.indexOf`. A plain object map or the `in` operator lets `'constructor'`, `'__proto__'` and `'toString'` match (AC-15).
- **Whitespace means `String.prototype.trim()` and nothing else.** NBSP and BOM are removed. Internal whitespace is not removed, so `'BBB +'` and `'B B'` are invalid.
- **Sign.** The result is `c - p`. `p - c` fails AC-4 and AC-5. Equal indexes give +0.
- **Missing or extra arguments.** A missing argument is `undefined` and throws `RangeError`. Arguments beyond two are ignored, for example `notchChange('A','A','x') === 0`.
- **Look-alike characters.** The Unicode minus U+2212, an en dash and the fullwidth plus U+FF0B are invalid, both in input and in the scale literal.
- **Both arguments invalid.** The error is raised for `previous` (AC-16).
- **Test discovery.** With no arguments, `npm test` (`node --test`) also finds `*.test.mjs` under `.work/` when it is run from the main checkout. AC-18 is therefore judged from the card's or job's checkout root.
